name: B-Roll Text Readability Sequence
use_when: A body section can be shown through B-roll while text names the emotional or story beat.
The B-roll is visually useful but too busy for text without treatment.
A short needs stronger story support than talking head plus captions.
avoid_when: The B-roll does not match the spoken idea.
The background treatment would hide important proof or action.
Centered text would block the subject's face, product, UI, or key action.

timeline_pattern.pattern: spoken_story_beat -> select_matching_broll -> trim_in_out -> place_text_above -> add_adjustment_layer_between -> darken_or_desaturate_broll -> extend_over_sequence
timeline_pattern.selection_rule: Choose B-roll by story beat, emotion, proof, or contrast rather than by whatever shot is available.
timeline_pattern.readability_rule: Darken, desaturate, dim, or blur only enough for the text to read.
timeline_pattern.source_monitor_rule: Mark in/out points before dropping B-roll so the selected moment matches the spoken beat.
timeline_pattern.whitespace_rule: Place text in the B-roll's usable negative space before dimming or covering the subject.

motion.rule: Keep B-roll motion subordinate to the text and spoken point; avoid busy camera movement behind small text.

keyframe_values.background_brightness: Lower brightness only as much as needed for text contrast; start with a mild reduction and check proof visibility.
keyframe_values.saturation: Reduce saturation when color competes with text, but preserve story-critical color information.
keyframe_values.text_position: Center text only when it does not hide the B-roll subject or action.
keyframe_values.line_breaks: Break text into readable phrases; do not let auto-wrap isolate filler words.

sound.rule: Mute or intentionally mix B-roll source audio under A-roll; do not leave accidental B-roll sound under speech.

captions.rule: Disable ordinary captions if the B-roll text carries the same phrase and would otherwise collide.

color.rule: Adjustment layers should improve text readability without making the B-roll look like an accidental grade mismatch.

implementation.ffmpeg: Trim B-roll with in/out metadata, apply eq/saturation filters for readability, overlay text, and preview at phone size.
implementation.remotion: Represent each B-roll text beat with sourceIn, sourceOut, text, adjustmentStyle, captionSuppression, and focalPoint fields.
implementation.blender: Use video planes with darkened material or overlay plane and text objects for stylized body sequences.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Trim the B-roll to the spoken beat, place text above it, add canvas/dim/adjust filters, and remove source audio if it fights dialogue.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Source Monitor I/O points, drag video-only when needed, place Essential Graphics text above B-roll, add an adjustment layer between text and B-roll, then reduce brightness and saturation with effects such as Brightness/Contrast and Lumetri.

common_mistakes: Using B-roll because the talking head has been onscreen too long rather than because the line needs it.
Darkening footage until the story detail is lost.
Leaving B-roll source audio under speech by accident.
Centering text over the exact subject the viewer should inspect.
Letting captions, B-roll text, and hook text compete at once.
Using text treatment to fix bad placement instead of moving the text into cleaner space.
qc: Each B-roll shot matches the spoken story beat.
Text remains readable at phone size.
Background treatment preserves necessary proof, action, and color detail.
Unwanted B-roll source audio is muted or intentionally mixed.
Captions and B-roll text do not duplicate or collide.
Text sits in negative space or a deliberate safe area rather than on top of the proof.
